The Triplet on Having the Path as Object (Maggārammaṇattika)
Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra):

Condition by Root (Hetupaccaya). Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object, a state that has the Path as its object arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate having the Path as its object, three aggregates [arise] …pe… dependent on two aggregates …pe….
Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, a state dominated by the Path arises by way of root condition:

dependent on one aggregate having the Path as its object, three aggregates dominated by the Path arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises. [Dependent on] two aggregates... [and so forth].

Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, states both having the Path as their object and dominated by the Path arise by way of root condition: [dependent on] a state having the Path as its object...
Dependent on one aggregate, there arise three aggregates that have the Path as their object and the Path as their predominance … two aggregates … [and so on].

Dependent on a state rooted in the Path, a state rooted in the Path arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate rooted in the Path, three aggregates arise … two aggregates … [and so on].

Dependent on a state rooted in the Path, a state with the Path as its predominance arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate rooted in the Path, three aggregates with the Path as their predominance arise … two aggregates … [and so on].
Dependent on a state conditioned by the Path, states conditioned by the Path and dominated by the Path arise by way of root condition:

dependent on one aggregate conditioned by the Path, three aggregates conditioned by the Path and dominated by the Path arise … two aggregates … [and so on] … Dependent on a state dominated by the Path, a state dominated by the Path arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate dominated by the Path, three aggregates arise … two aggregates … [and so on] …

Dependent on a state dominated by the Path, a state having the Path as its object arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate dominated by the Path, three aggregates having the Path as their object arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state dominated by the Path, a state rooted in the Path arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate dominated by the Path, three aggregates rooted in the Path arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on one aggregate, there arise three aggregates conditioned by the Path and dominated by the Path … two aggregates … [and so on] … Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object and is dominated by the Path,
a state that has the Path as its object arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate that has the Path as its object and is dominated by the Path, there arise three aggregates that have the Path as their object … two aggregates … [and so on] …
Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object and the Path as its dominant influence, a state that has the Path as its dominant influence arises by way of root condition:

dependent on one aggregate that has the Path as its object and the Path as its dominant influence, three aggregates that have the Path as their dominant influence arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] … Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object and the Path as its dominant influence, states that have the Path as their object and the Path as their dominant influence arise.

They arise by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate that has the Path as its object and the Path as its dominant influence, there arise three aggregates that have the Path as their object and the Path as their dominant influence … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state that has the Path as its root and the Path as its dominant influence, a state that has the Path as its root arises by way of root condition: [dependent on] a state that has the Path as its root and … [and so on] … the Path as its dominant influence.
Dependent on one aggregate dominated by the Path, there arise three aggregates conditioned by the Path … two aggregates … [and so on].
Dependent on a state conditioned by the Path and dominated by the Path, a state dominated by the Path arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate conditioned by the Path and dominated by the Path, three aggregates dominated by the Path arise … two aggregates … [and so on].

Dependent on a state that has the Path as its cause and the Path as its dominant factor, there arise states that have the Path as their cause and the Path as their dominant factor by way of the root condition:

dependent on one aggregate that has the Path as its cause and the Path as its dominant factor, there arise three aggregates that have the Path as their cause and the Path as their dominant factor; ... [and so on] ... dependent on two aggregates, ... [and so on] ....
Object, etc.:

dependent on a state having the Path as its object, a state having the Path as its object arises by way of object-condition … by way of predominance-condition … by way of proximity-condition … by way of contiguity-condition … by way of conascence-condition … by way of mutuality-condition … by way of support-condition.

… by way of decisive support condition … by way of prenascence condition … by way of repetition condition … by way of kamma condition … by way of nutriment condition … by way of faculty condition … by way of jhāna condition … by way of path condition … by way of association condition … by way of dissociation condition … by way of presence condition … by way of absence condition … by way of disappearance condition … by way of non-disappearance condition.
In the Pure Conditioned-Origination Enumeration Chapter:
there are seventeen [conditions] for the root condition; for the object, predominance, contiguity, immediate, conascence, mutuality, and dependence conditions...

In the case of strong-dependence, prenascence, repetition, kamma, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, association, dissociation, presence, absence, disappearance, and non-disappearance, there are seventeen [conditions]. (Thus they should be counted.
This is the Positive (Anuloma).
1.17.1.2. Analysis of the Negative Section on Conditions (Paccayapaccanīya Vibhaṅgavāra):
Not-root (Nahetu)

Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, a state having the Path as its object arises by way of the not-root condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate having the Path as its object, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….
Not-predominance:

Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, a state having the Path as its object arises by way of the not-predominance condition: dependent on one aggregate having the Path as its object, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, a state dominated by the Path arises by way of the not-predominance condition: dependent on one aggregate having the Path as its object, three aggregates dominated by the Path arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….
Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, states both having the Path as their object and dominated by the Path arise by way of the not-predominance condition:

dependent on one aggregate having the Path as its object, three aggregates both having the Path as their object and dominated by the Path arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state conditioned by the Path, a state conditioned by the Path arises by way of the not-predominance condition: dependent on the aggregates conditioned by the Path, the predominance conditioned by the Path [arises].

Dependent on a state conditioned by the Path, a state predominant by the Path arises by way of the not-predominance condition: dependent on the aggregates conditioned by the Path, the predominance that is predominant by the Path [arises].

Dependent on a state conditioned by the Path (maggahetuka), states conditioned by the Path and dominated by the Path arise by way of the not-dominance condition (na-adhipati-paccaya): dependent on the aggregates conditioned by the Path, there arises the dominance conditioned by the Path and dominated by the Path.
Dependent on a state dominated by the Path (maggādhipati), a state dominated by the Path arises by way of the not-dominance condition:
dependent on the aggregates dominated by the Path, there arises the dominance dominated by the Path. Dependent on one aggregate dominated by the Path, three aggregates [arise].
... pe ... two aggregates ... pe ...

Dependent on a state dominated by the Path, there arises a state having the Path as its object, by way of the not-predominance condition: dependent on one aggregate dominated by the Path, three aggregates having the Path as their object arise ... pe ... two aggregates ... pe ...

Dependent on a state dominated by the Path, there arises a state rooted in the Path, by way of the not-predominance condition: the predominance rooted in the Path arises dependent on the aggregates dominated by the Path.
Dependent on a state dominated by the Path, states that have the Path as their object and are dominated by the Path arise by way of the not-dominance condition:
dependent on one aggregate dominated by the Path, three aggregates that have the Path as their object and are dominated by the Path arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state dominated by the Path, states that are rooted in the Path and are dominated by the Path arise by way of the not-dominance condition: dependent on aggregates dominated by the Path, there arises the dominance that is both rooted in the Path and dominated by the Path.

Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object and the Path as its dominant factor, there arises a state that has the Path as its object, by way of the not-dominance condition: dependent on one aggregate that has the Path as its object and the Path as its dominant factor, there arise three aggregates that have the Path as their object … [and so on] … two aggregates … [and so on] …. Dependent on one aggregate dominated by the Path, there arise three aggregates dominated by the Path … two aggregates … [and so on] … Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object and is dominated by the Path,
states that have the Path as their object and are dominated by the Path arise by way of the not-dominance condition—
dependent on one aggregate that has the Path as its object and is dominated by the Path … [and so on].
The three aggregates that have the Path as their object and the Path as their dominant [condition] … [and so on] … two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state that has the Path as its cause and the Path as its dominant [condition], a state that has the Path as its cause arises by way of the non-dominant condition: dependent on the aggregates that have the Path as their cause and the Path as their dominant [condition], there arises the dominant [condition] that has the Path as its cause.

Dependent on a state that has the Path as its cause and the Path as its dominant [condition], a state that has the Path as its dominant [condition] arises by way of the non-dominant condition: dependent on the aggregates that have the Path as their cause and the Path as their dominant [condition], there arises the dominant [condition] that has the Path as its dominant [condition].

Dependent on states that have the Path as their cause and the Path as their dominating factor, there arise states that have the Path as their cause and the Path as their dominating factor by way of the non-dominating condition:

dependent on aggregates that have the Path as their cause and the Path as their dominating factor, there arises the dominating factor that has the Path as its cause and the Path as its dominating factor.

Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object, by way of not-prenascence condition, there arises a state that has the Path as its object... by way of not-postnascence condition. (Both [formulas] are complete.
Not-repetition.

Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, a state having the Path as its object arises by way of not-repetition condition: dependent on one aggregate having the Path as its object, three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates … [and so on].

Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, a state dominated by the Path arises by way of not-repetition condition: dependent on one aggregate having the Path as its object, three aggregates dominated by the Path arise … two aggregates … [and so on].
Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, states having the Path as their object and having the Path as their predominance arise by way of not-repetition condition:

dependent on one aggregate having the Path as its object, three aggregates having the Path as their object and having the Path as their predominance arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state having the Path as its predominance, a state having the Path as its predominance arises by way of not-repetition condition: dependent on one aggregate having the Path as its predominance, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state dominated by the Path, arises a state having the Path as its object, by way of not-repetition condition: dependent on one aggregate dominated by the Path, arise three aggregates having the Path as their object; ... two aggregates ... [and so on].
Dependent on a state dominated by the Path, arise states both having the Path as their object and dominated by the Path, by way of not-repetition condition:
dependent on one aggregate dominated by the Path, arise three aggregates both having the Path as their object and dominated by the Path; ... two aggregates ... [and so on].
Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object and the Path as its predominance, a state that has the Path as its object arises by way of the not-repetition condition:
dependent on one aggregate that has the Path as its object and the Path as its predominance, three aggregates that have the Path as their object arise … [and so on] … two aggregates … [and so on] ….

Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object and the Path as its predominance, a state that has the Path as its predominance arises by way of the not-repetition condition: [dependent on] a state that has the Path as its object and … [and so on] … the Path as its predominance.
Dependent on one aggregate dominated by the Path, there arise three aggregates dominated by the Path … two aggregates … [and so on].

Dependent on a state that has the Path as its object and is dominated by the Path, there arise states that have the Path as their object and are dominated by the Path by way of not-repetition condition:
dependent on one aggregate that has the Path as its object and is dominated by the Path … [and so on].
The three aggregates that have the Path as their object and the Path as their predominant factor … [and so on] … two aggregates … [and so on] ….
Not-kamma Condition:

Dependent on a state with the Path as its object, a state with the Path as its object arises by way of not-kamma condition—dependent on aggregates with the Path as their object, volition with the Path as its object arises.

Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, a state dominated by the Path arises by way of not-kamma-condition: dependent on aggregates having the Path as their object, volition dominated by the Path arises.

Dependent on a state having the Path as its object, states both having the Path as their object and dominated by the Path arise by way of not-kamma-condition: dependent on aggregates having the Path as their object, volition both having the Path as its object and dominated by the Path arises.

Dependent on a state conditioned by the Path, a state conditioned by the Path arises by way of not-kamma condition: dependent on the aggregates conditioned by the Path, volition conditioned by the Path arises.

Dependent on a state conditioned by the Path, a state dominated by the Path arises by way of not-kamma condition: dependent on the aggregates conditioned by the Path, volition dominated by the Path arises.

noble ones, having emerged from the Path, review the Path; they know the mind of one possessing a mind rooted in the Path by means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds;
aggregates rooted in the Path are [objects] of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, and the knowledge of future existences.

Knowledge of the future is related to adverting by way of object condition.

Conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: Noble ones, having emerged from the path, esteem and review the path.

namely, proximity-decisive support and natural decisive support ... [etc. ... Natural decisive support:
review is related to review by way of decisive support condition.

States that have the Path as their root and the Path as their predominance are a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state that has the Path as its object. States that have the Path as their root and the Path as their predominance are a condition, by way of decisive support condition, for a state that has the Path as its root.
As for natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*): the first Path is [a condition] for the second Path... the third Path for the fourth.
It is a condition for the Path by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

The first path is related to the second path by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). The third path is related to the fourth path by way of decisive support condition.

As for objective decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*): Noble ones, having emerged from the path, esteem the path...
...having done so, they review it.

States with the Path as their root and with the Path as their dominant condition are related to states with the Path as their root and with the Path as their dominant condition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
As natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*): the first Path is [related] to the second Path ... and so forth.
The third path is a condition for the fourth path by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). Regarding repetition condition (*āsevana-paccaya*):

Aggregates having the Path as their object are related to subsequent aggregates having the Path as their object by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).
A state having the Path as its object is related to a state dominated by the Path (*maggādhipati*) by way of the condition of repetition.
[Kamma, etc.]

A state having the Path as its object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state having the Path as its object: co-nascent … [etc. (There are no asynchronous [conditions]; seventeen questions are to be formulated).
Nutriment, etc.:
A state having the Path as its object is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition … by way of faculty-condition, for a state having the Path as its object.

Condition … by way of jhāna-condition … by way of path-condition … by way of association-condition … by way of presence-condition (these seven conditions have seventeen questions similar to those for the root-cause) … by way of absence-condition … by way of disappearance-condition (similar to the immediate condition) … by way of non-disappearance-condition. (Seventeen questions.)

In the pure root condition of the Enumeration Chapter, there are seventeen; in the object condition, nine; in the predominance condition, twenty-one; in the proximity condition, nine; in the contiguity condition, nine.
In co-nascence, seventeen; in mutuality, seventeen; in dependence, seventeen; in strong-dependence, twenty-one; in repetition, nine; in kamma, seventeen;
in nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, and association, seventeen; in presence, seventeen; in absence, nine;
in disappearance, nine; in non-disappearance, seventeen. (Thus it should be counted.)
Positive order.

1.17.7.2. Negative Conditionality (*Paccayapaccanīya*)
In the Enumeration Chapter,
under the pure [classification], there are twenty-one for "not-root" and seventeen for "not-object" (when "not-object" is taken, both natural object and decisive support object are included).
Two [factors] are cut off; twenty-one [factors] do not [arise] by way of predominance, neither-proximity-nor-immediate, nor-conascence, nor-mutuality,
nor-dependence, nor-strong-dependence, nor-prenascence, nor-postnascence, nor-repetition,
nor-kamma, nor-resultant, nor-nutriment, nor-faculty, nor-jhāna, nor-path, nor-association, nor-dissociation, nor-presence, nor-absence, nor-disappearance.
In the non-repetition [formula], there are twenty-one. (It should be counted in this manner.
The Negative. 1.17.7.3.
Positive-Negative Condition.
Hetuduka: With root condition as the basis, there are seventeen [factors] that are not object, not predominance, not proximity, not contiguity,
not decisive support, not prenascence, not postnascence, not repetition, not kamma, not result, not nutriment, not faculty, not jhāna, and not path.
In the combination of non-disappearance, non-absence, and non-disappearance, there are seventeen [conditions]. (Thus it should be counted.
This is the Positive-Negative (Anulomapaccanīya).
1.17.7.4. Negative-Positive (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma)

In the "Not-root" dyad: with the not-root condition, there are nine [ways] in the object condition; twenty-one in the predominance condition; nine in the proximity condition; nine in the contiguity condition;
seventeen in the conascence condition; seventeen in the mutuality condition; seventeen in the dependence condition; twenty-one in the strong-dependence condition; [and] in the repetition condition...
Nine; with kamma, seventeen; with nutriment, seventeen; with faculty, jhāna, path, and association, seventeen;
with presence, seventeen; with absence, nine; with disappearance, nine; with non-disappearance, seventeen. (Thus it should be counted.
This is the Negative-Positive (Paccanīyānuloma).
The triad with the Path as object is finished.
